If $u=1, l=0, r=0$, $k=5$. Path: A4 -> B4 -> B3 -> A3 -> A4 (revisit!) or A4 -> B4 -> C4 -> B4 (revisit!).

- $P(G,n)$ is the set of partitions $\sigma$ of $[n]$ such that $\bot_n \leq^\ast_G \sigma$.
- $\bot_n$ is the all-singleton partition.
- $\rho \leq_G \sigma$ if $\sigma$ is obtained by merging two blocks $B_i, B_j$ of $\rho$ that have an edge between them in $G$.
- $\leq^\ast_G$ is the reflexive-transitive closure.

- A partition $\sigma$ is in $P(G,n)$ if and only if each block of $\sigma$ induces a connected subgraph of $G$.
- This is because starting from singletons, merging blocks with an edge creates connected components. Any connected subgraph can be built this way.
- The poset is the set of partitions whose blocks are connected subgraphs, ordered by refinement.
- This is exactly the lattice of flats of the graphic matroid $M(G)$.
- The lattice of flats of any matroid is a geometric lattice.
- It is not necessarily a total order.
